description: A budget line with `spent` = 0 means nothing has been spent yet, so it is left out of the rate averages.

d.request: For each event type, calculate the average spending rate by first computing each event's mean of (spent ÷ amount) across its budget lines excluding those with spent = 0, then averaging these event-level rates by type, and finally dividing each type's average by the mean of all type-level averages.
d.sql:
WITH budget_rates AS (
  SELECT 
    b.link_to_event,
    e.type,
    CAST(b.spent AS FLOAT) / CAST(b.amount AS FLOAT) AS rate
  FROM budget b
  JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
  WHERE b.spent > 0 AND b.amount > 0
),
event_avg_rates AS (
  SELECT 
    link_to_event,
    type,
    AVG(rate) AS event_rate
  FROM budget_rates
  GROUP BY link_to_event, type
),
type_avg_rates AS (
  SELECT 
    type,
    AVG(event_rate) AS type_rate
  FROM event_avg_rates
  GROUP BY type
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(type_rate) AS overall_avg
  FROM type_avg_rates
)
SELECT 
  t.type,
  t.type_rate,
  (SELECT overall_avg FROM overall_mean) AS overall_average,
  t.type_rate / (SELECT overall_avg FROM overall_mean) AS normalized_rate
FROM type_avg_rates t
ORDER BY t.type

b.request: Exclude budget lines with spent = 0 when calculating per-event average spending rates (spent ÷ amount) from matched budget-event lines, then for each event type average those event rates and display the type, its average spending rate, and that rate divided by the mean of all per-type rates.
b.sql: WITH budget_with_rate AS (SELECT b.budget_id, b.link_to_event, CAST(b.spent AS FLOAT) / b.amount AS spending_rate FROM budget b WHERE b.spent > 0), event_avg_rate AS (SELECT link_to_event, AVG(spending_rate) AS event_avg_rate FROM budget_with_rate GROUP BY link_to_event), type_avg_rate AS (SELECT e.type, AVG(ear.event_avg_rate) AS type_avg_rate FROM event_avg_rate ear JOIN event e ON ear.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.type), overall_mean AS (SELECT AVG(type_avg_rate) AS overall_mean_rate FROM type_avg_rate) SELECT tar.type, tar.type_avg_rate, tar.type_avg_rate / om.overall_mean_rate AS rate_divided_by_mean FROM type_avg_rate tar CROSS JOIN overall_mean om

c.request: Using budget lines matched to their event (drop lines with no matching event), work out for each event its average spending rate, `spent` ÷ `amount`, across its lines. Then, for each event `type`, average those event-level rates. Show the type, its average spending rate, and that rate divided by the simple mean of the per-type average rates. Ignore missing values in the averages, and don't round. A budget line with `spent` = 0 means nothing has been spent yet, so it is left out of the rate averages.
c.sql: WITH event_rates AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.type, AVG(CAST(b.spent AS REAL) / CAST(b.amount AS REAL)) as avg_rate FROM budget b JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE b.spent > 0 GROUP BY e.event_id, e.type), type_rates AS (SELECT type, AVG(avg_rate) as type_avg_rate FROM event_rates GROUP BY type), overall_mean AS (SELECT AVG(type_avg_rate) as overall_avg FROM type_rates) SELECT type, type_avg_rate, type_avg_rate / (SELECT overall_avg FROM overall_mean) as normalized_rate FROM type_rates

a.request: Using budget lines matched to their event (drop lines with no matching event), work out for each event its average spending rate, `spent` ÷ `amount`, across its lines, leaving out lines where `spent` is 0. Then, for each event `type`, average those event-level rates. Return the type, its average spending rate, and that rate divided by the simple mean of the per-type average rates. Ignore missing values in the averages, and don't round.
a.sql: WITH event_level AS (SELECT b.link_to_event, e.type, AVG(CASE WHEN b.spent > 0 THEN b.spent / b.amount ELSE NULL END) as event_avg_rate FROM budget b INNER JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY b.link_to_event, e.type), type_level AS (SELECT type, AVG(event_avg_rate) as type_avg_rate FROM event_level GROUP BY type), overall_stats AS (SELECT AVG(type_avg_rate) as overall_mean FROM type_level) SELECT type_level.type, type_level.type_avg_rate, type_level.type_avg_rate / overall_stats.overall_mean as normalized_rate FROM type_level CROSS JOIN overall_stats
